critical_operation.code_excerpt:
#  define LEAD_CASE(n)                                                         \
  case BT_LEAD##n:                                                             \
    if (end - ptr < n)                                                         \
      return XML_TOK_PARTIAL_CHAR;                                             \
    if (IS_NMSTRT_CHAR(enc, ptr, n)) {                                         \
critical_operation.description: In the prolog tokenizer, a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence (BT_LEAD2/3/4) is tested with IS_NMSTRT_CHAR and IS_NAME_CHAR but never with IS_INVALID_CHAR. The encoding's name-character test can therefore accept a byte sequence that is structurally invalid for the declared encoding. The same omission exists in the CHECK_NAME_CASE and CHECK_NMSTRT_CASE macros used by the other tokenizers. The fix inserts IS_INVALID_CHAR(enc, ptr, n) before each name-character check, so an invalid encoding is rejected as XML_TOK_INVALID instead of being consumed as a name. This is the missing validation described by CVE-2022-25235; the advisory groups three hunks in xmltok_impl.c.

entry_point.description: The prolog tokenizer receives attacker-controlled bytes from the XML parser before any document-level validation.
